goal: Remove every external messaging surface from CGKN Codex Edition and retain only the active Codex conversation without weakening Provider, evidence, packaging, or delivery authority boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical user review and delivery receipts use Codex conversation, turn, reviewer, event, and artifact identities.

No active source, launcher, configuration, schema, documentation, or test path contains an external chat transport, conversation credential, polling service, secondary UI, or messaging delivery behavior.
Provider output validation, post-build finalization, canonical evidence, local_packager, public delivery gate, and delivery manifest remain one governed route.
Static removal checks, schema validation, kernel guards, and the focused regression suite pass.
Documentation describes the active Codex task as the only user interaction surface and no separate launcher is required.
Whiteboard and agent_session remain the shared project communication state.

quality_metrics.measure: management artifacts conform to registered JSON schemas and semantic invariants
quality_metrics.target: all management, iteration, and experience artifacts validate
quality_metrics.method: jsonschema tests plus deterministic manager validation

quality_metrics.measure: formal provider and delivery route preservation
quality_metrics.target: kernel and provider contract tests pass without a new generation or delivery path
quality_metrics.method: existing kernel and formal provider test profiles

quality_metrics.measure: bounded Codex escalation usefulness and authority isolation
quality_metrics.target: a librarian-curated request and Codex response stay within configured budgets, preserve request identity, produce actionable guidance, and cannot assert formal evidence or delivery authority
quality_metrics.method: schema validation, deterministic contract tests, support-pipeline prompt tests, and an offline failed-generation replay

prevention: Confirm acceptance, interfaces, and applicable kernel constraints before implementation.
assurance: Review method, schema, skill, and repository instruction consistency.
Validate that support artifacts cannot authorize formal delivery PASS.
Review changed files against the kernel contract before integration.
control: Run targeted kernel and knowledge tests.
improvement: Record review findings and one bounded improvement experiment.

interface_expectations: scripts.codex_conversation is import-only and projects all user-visible text and local artifacts into the active Codex task.
Canonical review uses conversation_id, reviewer_id, event_id, turn_id, and turn_date from the active Codex turn.
Canonical delivery receipts bind conversation_id, turn_id, artifact_id, and artifact_unique_id without accepting a bare boolean send result.
The runtime supervisor processes identity-bound checkpoints but does not own or launch a second conversation service.
Provider validation, post-build finalization, local_packager, public_delivery_gate, and delivery_manifest.json remain the only public delivery route.

feedback: Codex-only interaction, identity migration, and governed delivery-route preservation passed the focused regression and static removal checks.

worked: Separating the in-process Codex projection from Provider, evidence, packaging, and delivery authority made the transport removal bounded and testable.
did_not_work: Transport-shaped fixtures and historical generated evidence initially retained obsolete names; explicit Codex identity fixtures and a full tracked-text guard corrected them.
experiments: Keep the Codex-only repository scan in the default test profile and reject any future detached conversation launcher or credential.
